_comment: Hand-authored sub-patterns that none of the seven curated sheets names, but that
interviewers do. Merged into patterns/<id>.md by scripts/augment-briefs.py alongside
the sheet-derived ones, so a hand edit to a brief is never silently regenerated away.
Add an entry only when the technique has a distinct RECOGNITION SIGNAL. If the signal
is the same as an existing row, it is the same sub-pattern under another name.

01-arrays-hashing.name: Suffix Sum / Suffix Max
01-arrays-hashing.recognize: The answer at index i depends on everything to its RIGHT — 'product of all except self', 'can I reach the end', 'best trade after this day'
01-arrays-hashing.strategy: Sweep right-to-left accumulating the running total or running max into a suffix array, then combine with the prefix sweep in a second pass. Two passes, O(n), no nested loop
01-arrays-hashing.why: The mirror of prefix sum, and the half people forget. Learners who only know prefix sum solve the left-to-right variants and stall on the rest.

01-arrays-hashing.name: Prefix XOR
01-arrays-hashing.recognize: Range query over XOR instead of sum — 'xor of subarray', 'subarrays with xor equal to k'
01-arrays-hashing.strategy: XOR is its own inverse, so the same prefix trick works with XOR in place of subtraction: xor[i..j] = pre[j] ^ pre[i-1]
01-arrays-hashing.why: The identity that makes it work is not obvious, and it is the whole problem.

01-arrays-hashing.name: Difference Array
01-arrays-hashing.recognize: Many range UPDATES then one final read — 'add val to every index in [l, r]', 'car pooling', 'corporate flight bookings'
01-arrays-hashing.strategy: Record only the boundaries of each update (+val at l, -val at r+1), then one prefix-sum pass at the end turns the boundary marks into the final array. O(1) per update instead of O(r-l)
01-arrays-hashing.why: The inverse of prefix sum, and the reason a range-update problem is not O(n*q).

01-arrays-hashing.name: 2-D Prefix Sum
01-arrays-hashing.recognize: Repeated sum over a RECTANGLE of a grid — 'sum of submatrix', 'matrix block sum', many queries on a static matrix
01-arrays-hashing.strategy: Build a cumulative grid where each cell holds the sum of everything above-and-left, then any rectangle is four lookups by inclusion-exclusion
01-arrays-hashing.why: The inclusion-exclusion step is where this is got wrong, and it generalises the 1-D idea rather than replacing it.

02-two-pointers.name: Dutch National Flag / 3-Way Partition
02-two-pointers.recognize: Sort or group into exactly THREE categories in one pass, in place — 'sort colors', 'partition around a pivot value'
02-two-pointers.strategy: Three pointers: a low boundary, a high boundary, and a scanner. Swap the scanned element to whichever boundary it belongs to and move only the pointers that are safe to move
02-two-pointers.why: The classic trap is advancing the scanner after a swap with the high boundary, which skips an unexamined element.

02-two-pointers.name: Cyclic Sort
02-two-pointers.recognize: The values are a permutation of 1..n or 0..n-1 and the problem asks for a missing, duplicate, or misplaced number — and wants O(1) extra space
02-two-pointers.strategy: Each value has exactly one correct home index. Repeatedly swap the current element to its home until the position is settled, then a single scan reveals whichever index disagrees with its value
02-two-pointers.why: Recognising it from the CONSTRAINT ('values in range 1..n') rather than the wording is the transferable skill.
